control_point: Unique Transaction Identifiers are generated, paired and matched with the counterparty and reported values are reconciled with the trade repository under EMIR REFIT.

citations.source_name: Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 (EMIR), Article 9 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2019/834 (EMIR REFIT)

Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2022/1855 supplementing EMIR with regard to regulatory technical standards on the procedures and arrangements for the registration and reconciliation of OTC derivative contracts

consequence_anchor.public_source: EMIR trade-repository reconciliation and pairing failure regime; competent authority powers under Article 21 of Regulation (EU) No 648/2012
consequence_anchor.magnitude_band: operational remediation cost plus potential public enforcement and corrective-order exposure; published supervisory fines in the multi-million-euro range for persistent reporting failures

commonality_rationale: Every EU-obligated derivatives counterparty must generate or obtain a UTI, pair it with its counterparty and reconcile reportable fields with a registered trade repository; the requirement is asset-class-agnostic and applies across cleared and uncleared OTC derivatives.
